---
id: "smk-07"
title: "The Rhine"
---

The Rhine is one of the major rivers of Western Europe. It begins in the Swiss Alps, flows through Lake Constance, forms part of the border between Switzerland and Germany, and then runs north through the Upper Rhine Plain past Basel, Strasbourg, Mainz and Cologne before crossing the Netherlands and reaching the North Sea near Rotterdam. Its length is roughly 1,230 kilometres. The Rhine is among the busiest waterways in the world: barges carry coal, ore, chemicals and containers between the port of Rotterdam and the industrial regions of Germany and Switzerland. The stretch between Bingen and Koblenz, the Rhine Gorge, is famous for its castles and vineyards and is a World Heritage Site. Important tributaries include the Aare, the Neckar, the Main and the Moselle. Flooding, water quality and the migration of salmon have been the subject of international agreements among the countries of the basin.
